High-speed steel needs a grade-specific heat-treatment schedule. Credit answers that:
- identify the exact high-speed-steel grade and follow its manufacturer’s heat-treatment data
- use the specified preheating and austenitising stages, holding times and cooling method
- temper at the grade’s stated high-speed-steel temperature, normally in repeated cycles
- explain that hardening provides wear resistance and tempering provides sufficient toughness

Do not credit a 150–250 °C straw temper as the standard treatment for high-speed steel; it is not a general high-speed-steel schedule.

practice_questions.text:
Which one of the following correctly describes hot-dip galvanising?
A) Steel is coated with chromium using electrolysis in a plating bath
B) Steel is immersed in molten zinc at approximately 450 °C to form a zinc-iron alloy layer
C) Steel is heated and dipped into a fluidised bed of thermoplastic powder
D) Steel is spray-painted with a zinc-rich primer to prevent rust
practice_questions.marks: B) Steel is immersed in molten zinc at approximately 450 °C to form a zinc-iron alloy layer [1 mark]

practice_questions.text: Explain why galvanising provides better corrosion protection than painting when the surface coating is scratched.
practice_questions.marks:
Galvanising: zinc is more electrochemically active than iron [1 mark], so when a scratch exposes bare steel, the surrounding zinc corrodes preferentially (sacrificial protection) and the steel is protected; with paint, a scratch exposes bare steel directly to moisture and corrosion spreads under the surrounding film [1 mark].
[2 marks]

practice_questions.text: Describe the stages of the dip coating process for a set of wire dishwasher racks.
practice_questions.type: 4 marks — Describe Stages of a Process
practice_questions.marks:
Award one mark each for any four of:
- Clean and degrease the wire racks thoroughly (remove grease, rust and scale)
- Heat the racks in an oven to approximately 200 °C
- Dip the heated racks into a fluidised bed of thermoplastic powder (e.g. PVC or polyethylene)
- The hot metal melts the powder particles on contact, building up a thick coating
- Remove racks and cure in oven to flow and consolidate the coating
- Allow to cool; inspect the finished coating for voids or thin spots
[4 marks]

practice_questions.text: Identify one surface finishing method suitable for protecting an aluminium bicycle component and explain why it is appropriate for aluminium.
practice_questions.marks:
Anodising [1 mark].
Anodising uses electrolysis to thicken the natural oxide layer that forms on aluminium; the anodised layer is hard, scratch-resistant and cannot peel because it is part of the aluminium itself; it can also be dyed to give a colour finish, which is desirable for a bicycle component [1 mark for appropriate explanation].
[2 marks — accept also: painting/dip coating with explanation; do not accept electroplating with chromium as primary answer without qualification]

practice_questions.text:
Crestfield Street Furniture Ltd manufactures steel litter bins and benches for installation in coastal seaside towns. Salt spray, moisture and vandalism are key hazards. The production manager is evaluating whether to use hot-dip galvanising or dip coating as the primary protection method.

Evaluate which surface finishing method is more suitable for this application. In your answer, consider corrosion protection mechanism, impact resistance, appearance, cost and any limitations of each method.
practice_questions.type: 8 marks — Extended Response: Evaluate an Engineering Decision
practice_questions.marks:
Mastering (7-8 marks): Balanced evaluation with clear links to the scenario (coastal salt spray, vandalism, litter bins and benches). Both processes evaluated on multiple criteria with similarities and differences noted. Justified conclusion.

Secure (5-6 marks): Most criteria covered for both processes. Some comparison made. Conclusion present but may lack full justification.

Developing (3-4 marks): One process described in more detail. Limited comparison. Scenario details used minimally.

Emerging (1-2 marks): Generic points about surface finishing with little or no link to the scenario.

Content that may be credited:
Galvanising: zinc sacrificial protection works even if the surface is scratched by vandalism — corrodes preferentially over steel; excellent for the coastal/salt environment; produces a dull grey metallic appearance (not ideal for decorative street furniture); thick zinc-iron alloy bond is robust; relatively low cost per tonne of steel treated in large galvanising bath; difficult to apply to assembled structures with tight spaces.
Dip coating: thick thermoplastic coat (1–3 mm) resists impact from vandalism without cracking or chipping; available in a range of colours for aesthetic appearance; good chemical resistance to salt and moisture; does not offer sacrificial protection (once scratched through to bare steel, corrosion can spread); requires heating components, so very large assembled units may be impractical; more expensive per part than galvanising for large structural sections.
Similarities: both processes protect steel from corrosion; both require surface preparation before application; both suit factory-applied batch production.
Conclusion: for this coastal application, a combined approach (galvanise first for sacrificial protection, then powder coat or dip coat for appearance and impact resistance) is ideal. If only one process is chosen, galvanising is the better primary corrosion protector in a coastal salt-spray environment.

practice_questions.text: Compare electroplating and spray painting as surface finishing methods for a decorative steel tap. In your answer, consider the process, coating thickness, surface finish quality, cost and durability.
practice_questions.type: 6 marks — Compare Two Processes or Methods
practice_questions.marks:
Process: electroplating uses electrolysis to deposit chromium or nickel from a plating bath; spray painting uses compressed air to apply a liquid coating.
Coating thickness: electroplating deposits a very thin layer (1–50 micrometres) with dimensional precision; spray paint is thinner than dip coating but thicker than plating (50–150 micrometres typically).
Surface finish: electroplating gives a mirror-bright finish with high uniformity; spray paint can be high-gloss but is more susceptible to runs and orange-peel texture if poorly applied.
Cost: electroplating equipment and effluent management are expensive; spray painting is lower capital cost for small volumes.
Durability: chromium electroplating is very hard and scratch-resistant; paint can chip, allowing corrosion to undercut the coating. For a bathroom tap (damp environment, frequent contact), electroplating is significantly more durable.
[6 marks — 1 mark per valid point; 2 marks for a developed comparative point. No marks for describing each in isolation without comparison.]

practice_questions.text:
Which one of the following best describes a microcontroller?
A) A type of logic gate used to invert a signal
B) A single chip containing a processor, memory and programmable I/O connections
C) A relay that switches between mains and battery power
D) A sensor that converts temperature to a digital signal
practice_questions.marks: B) A single chip containing a processor, memory and programmable I/O connections [1 mark]

practice_questions.text:
A microcontroller is used in an automatic plant-watering system. A soil moisture sensor is the input; a water pump motor is the output.

The system must switch the pump ON when the moisture reading falls below a set threshold, and switch it OFF when the reading is at or above the threshold.

Draw and label a flowchart for this system. Your flowchart must include: START, reading the sensor, a decision, switching the pump on or off, and a loop back.
practice_questions.type: 5 marks — Complete the Flowchart or System Diagram
practice_questions.marks:
Award marks for:
- START terminator (oval) present [1 mark]
- 'Read soil moisture sensor' in a parallelogram [1 mark]
- Decision diamond: 'Is moisture below threshold?' (or equivalent) with YES and NO branches [1 mark]
- YES branch: 'Switch pump ON'; NO branch: 'Switch pump OFF' (or vice versa — check logic is consistent) [1 mark]
- Feedback loop back to 'Read sensor' from both branches (continuous control loop) [1 mark]
[5 marks]

practice_questions.text: State two advantages of using a microcontroller to control an automated system instead of using a fixed logic gate circuit.
practice_questions.marks:
Award 1 mark per advantage, up to 2 marks:
- A microcontroller can be reprogrammed to change its behaviour without rewiring or replacing hardware.
- A single microcontroller can handle many inputs and outputs with complex decision logic that would require numerous discrete logic gate ICs.
- Built-in timing and ADC functions remove the need for separate timer ICs and converter chips.
- The same microcontroller hardware can be reused for different products by changing only the program.
[2 marks — vague answers like 'easier' without specifying the mechanism do not earn marks]

practice_questions.text: Explain why a transistor or FET is needed between a microcontroller output pin and a DC motor. In your answer, refer to current.
practice_questions.marks:
Award 1 mark per correct point, up to 2 marks:
- A microcontroller output pin can only supply a small current (typically 20-40 mA), which is not enough to drive a motor.
- A transistor or FET is used as a switch: a small control current/voltage on the base/gate switches a much larger current through the motor.
- Without the interfacing component, the large motor current would damage or destroy the microcontroller.
[2 marks — must mention small control current vs large motor current]

practice_questions.text:
A light-sensing system uses an LDR, a microcontroller and an LED indicator. The LDR is connected to the microcontroller via an ADC. The system must switch the LED on when light levels are low.

Describe the four stages that happen between the LDR detecting a change in light level and the LED switching on.
practice_questions.type: 4 marks — Describe Stages of a Process
practice_questions.marks:
Award 1 mark per correct stage, up to 4 marks:
1. The LDR resistance increases as light falls, changing the analogue voltage in the sensing circuit.
2. The ADC converts this analogue voltage into a digital number (e.g. 0-1023).
3. The microcontroller program compares the digital number to the stored threshold value.
4. If the reading is below the threshold, the program sets the output pin HIGH, which switches the LED on (via a transistor/directly if current is within limit).
[4 marks]

practice_questions.text:
Aethon Robotics is designing an automated greenhouse monitoring system. The system monitors temperature and humidity using two analogue sensors, and controls a heating element, a ventilation fan and a misting pump. The lead engineer proposes using a microcontroller rather than separate logic gate circuits for each function.

Evaluate this proposal. Consider advantages and disadvantages of using a microcontroller for this application.
practice_questions.type: 8 marks — Extended Response: Evaluate an Engineering Decision
practice_questions.marks:
Mastering (7-8): Detailed evaluation. Advantages: single chip handles all three output devices and two sensor inputs (within the three-inputs/three-outputs model if temperature and humidity are the two active inputs); reprogrammable — thresholds and timing can be adjusted for different crops without hardware changes; built-in ADC converts analogue sensor outputs; timing control allows delays (e.g. fan runs for 30 s after triggering). Disadvantages: program must be written and tested; if the microcontroller fails, all three functions stop; needs correct interfacing components for high-current actuators (heater, fan, pump). Compares with discrete approach (very complex wiring, not reprogrammable, harder to modify). Reaches justified conclusion referencing the greenhouse context.

Secure (5-6): Identifies key advantages (reprogrammable, handles multiple I/O) and at least one disadvantage. Some comparison with alternative. Conclusion present.

Developing (3-4): Describes microcontroller function and one or two advantages. Limited evaluation depth.

Emerging (1-2): Basic description of what a microcontroller is with minimal evaluative comment.

[8 marks]

practice_questions.text:
Which one of the following correctly describes a dead load on a structure?
A) A load caused by vehicles and people using the structure
B) A suddenly applied impact force such as a collision
C) The permanent weight of the structure itself and fixed components
D) A force that changes direction 50 times per second
practice_questions.marks: C) The permanent weight of the structure itself and fixed components [1 mark]

practice_questions.text:
State the type of internal force experienced by each of the following structural members:
(a) A suspension bridge cable supporting the deck
(b) A stone arch in a bridge
(c) A long, thin steel column that collapses sideways under load
practice_questions.marks:
(a) Tension [1 mark — NOT compression; cables only pull]
(b) Compression [1 mark]
(c) Buckling [1 mark]
[3 marks]

practice_questions.text:
A hydraulic car jack has an input piston with an area of 0.005 m² and an output piston with an area of 0.05 m². The mechanic applies a force of 200 N to the input piston.

Calculate the output force produced by the jack.
practice_questions.marks:
Formula: F2 = F1 × A2/A1 [1 mark]
Substitution: F2 = 200 × 0.05/0.005 [1 mark]
= 200 × 10 [1 mark for correct ratio]
= 2000 N [1 mark for correct final answer with unit]
[4 marks — method marks awarded even if arithmetic error; penalise if unit missing from final answer]

practice_questions.text: Give two differences between a pneumatic system and a hydraulic system. For each difference, explain how it affects the choice of system for a particular engineering application.
practice_questions.type: 6 marks — Compare Two Processes or Methods
practice_questions.marks:
Mastering (5-6): Two clear differences, each with an application-linked explanation:
- Pneumatic uses compressible air (fast-acting, lower maximum force); hydraulic uses incompressible oil (precise, very high force). Example: pneumatic for robot grippers and packaging machines where speed matters; hydraulic for excavator arms and car brakes where high force or precision is critical.
- Pneumatic is cleaner (no risk of oil leaks); hydraulic risk of fluid contamination. Example: pneumatic preferred in food/pharma environments; hydraulic acceptable in outdoor heavy plant.
- Pneumatic cylinders extend quickly due to air compression; hydraulic extends more slowly but with greater control.
Both differences must explicitly link to an application.

Secure (3-4): Two differences identified with partial application links. May lack specificity in the application context.

Developing (2): One difference with a brief application link.

Emerging (1): One difference named with no application link.

[6 marks]

practice_questions.text: Describe the function of a 5/2 directional control valve in a pneumatic circuit that controls a double-acting cylinder.
practice_questions.marks:
Award 1 mark per correct point, up to 2 marks:
- A 5/2 valve has five ports (air inlet, two cylinder ports, two exhaust ports) and two switching positions.
- Switching from one position to the other directs compressed air to one side of the cylinder (extending the piston) while venting the other side to exhaust, and vice versa when switched back (retracting the piston).
[2 marks]

practice_questions.text:
Marrowbone Engineering manufactures industrial clamping equipment. The design team must choose between a pneumatic clamping system and a hydraulic clamping system for a new metal-forming press that must apply a clamping force of 50,000 N.

Evaluate which system is better suited to this application. In your answer, refer to Pascal's law and the properties of the fluids involved.
practice_questions.type: 8 marks — Extended Response: Evaluate an Engineering Decision
practice_questions.marks:
Mastering (7-8): Explains Pascal's law (pressure transmitted equally in enclosed fluid, allowing force amplification via F2 = F1 × A2/A1). Shows that both systems can amplify force, but a 50,000 N requirement is very high. Evaluates hydraulic: oil is incompressible — force is transmitted precisely and consistently at very high levels; force amplification is reliable and predictable; used in heavy presses and brakes for these reasons; disadvantage: oil leak risk, higher cost, maintenance of seals. Evaluates pneumatic: air is compressible — force output fluctuates slightly with air consumption; achieving 50,000 N with air pressure alone would require very large cylinder area or very high operating pressure (safety concern); advantage: cleaner, cheaper. Concludes hydraulic is more appropriate for this application with clear reasoning.

Secure (5-6): Correctly identifies hydraulic as better for high-force application. Mentions incompressibility of hydraulic fluid and compressibility of air. Some reference to force amplification principle. Conclusion present with reasoning.

Developing (3-4): States hydraulic is better with a partial explanation of why. May mention force amplification without linking it to fluid compressibility.

Emerging (1-2): Identifies one of the two systems with minimal reasoning.

[8 marks]
